mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. This signal is active in all monetary regimes but most pronounced during easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points over three months signals labor market deterioration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as economic weakness becomes evident.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and real consumption (RSAFS) by more than 0.5% over two months indicate a broad-based demand slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by > 0.5% in 2 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation periods (CPIAUCSL 12-month change > 6.0%), the Federal Reserve's tightening policy leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as equity valuations face higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when CPIAUCSL 12-month change > 6.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening supply-side activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings face headwinds from reduced output.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when INDPRO declines by > 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) falling below 1500 thousand units signal a housing market contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer confidence and investment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1500.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% and 0.2 percentage points respectively over one month indicates a severe labor market crisis, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS declines by > 0.5% and UNRATE rises by > 0.2pp in 1 month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Slow GDP growth (GDPC1 quarterly growth rate < 1.0% annualized) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings growth decelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters when GDPC1 growth < 1.0% annualized, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
